scope: Read-only protocol and current published firmware/source inspection; no device execution.

conclusions.controllerId: Real protocol controller_id is already exposed as players[].controllerId. ESP32 ID derives from factory MAC; virtual SDK ID is per-instance virtual-<12 hex> and survives reconnect on the same instance.
conclusions.numericSeat: players[].id is a gameplay seat, not the device ID; session changes on reconnect and should not replace the displayed device ID.
conclusions.rssiReason: Published firmware message templates and SDK only send identity/keys/liveness; no RSSI telemetry. Repository includes merged firmware binary without firmware build sources.
conclusions.nonConsumingUiSource: Use GameKit observedControllers and legacy adapter.peek/currentInputs. Do not call native.snapshot a second time: it consumes button pulses.
conclusions.liveDisplay: Filter transport=wifi and connected=true; show a gamepad icon, player seat, and full controllerId via textContent. Keep the connected indicator visible even while 3D games hide QR instructions.

recommendedSignalUi: Hide strength when unreported or show a concise unavailable label; no fabricated bars, host-WiFi RSSI, heartbeat-derived RF strength, or RTT-derived RF strength.
checks: Connected controller ID follows actual protocol identity, not IP/seat/session.
Two seats show independent IDs, a disconnected seat cannot remain marked connected, same-ID reconnect retains correct seat.
Long accepted 96-character IDs wrap without clipping at 960x540 and 1280x720; use textContent rather than innerHTML.
UI does not poll the native snapshot again or consume short button pulses.
Connected badge remains visible during active 3D gameplay when QR instructions collapse.
RSSI absence does not produce a fabricated numeric value or strength bars; Chinese/English strings are consistent.
